# Code of Conduct

1. We are a rope-focused community group. Our main focus is hosting a regular peer learning event – this is not a play party unless explicitly stated otherwise.
2. Our events run on the premise of equality and respect and to this aim we reject racism, homophobia, sexism, transphobia, breaches of consent, body shaming, ableism and classism, in all forms whether they are blatant or come in the form of microaggressions.
3. Please do not assume anyone's gender or pronouns.
4. Do not touch another person, their rope or belongings without specific consent.
5. Please do not take photographs without the consent of everyone who would be in the image (including those in the background).
6. No full nudity or fetish wear, think comfy gym/dance gear.
7. We practice explicit, informed and embodied or enthusiastic consent (the spirit of this statement is more important than the specific vocabulary chosen to describe it). If you are unsure if consent has been given, seek clarification before proceeding.
8. The event safeword is Red. If this safeword is used and you do not move to end your tying, someone may intervene to make sure the safeword is being respected and acted upon.
9. We follow R.A.C.K (Risk Aware Consensual Kink) and believe nothing is inherently safe or without risk. With this in mind, please take responsibility for your own safety and those you are tying with. Have your own safety shears/equipment checked and to hand. We have no DM's, ask a community member to be a spotter if required and clearly specify what you need from them if you do so. Be upfront in negotiations regarding any health and safety issues relating to your tying.
10. Respect other peoples' scenes. Although we are a learning space please do not interrupt to ask questions or give suggestions unless you have negotiated permission or there are immediate safety concerns, maintain a respectful distance and ask before actively spectating. This applies for partnered and self-tying.
11. Our environment is a relaxed one, and socialising is part of what makes us a community, but please be mindful of volume levels near others tying.
12. This event is a sober event. Please do not arrive in an altered state or consume substances such as alcohol or drugs at the event.
13. If you have any concerns or questions, there are allocated 'feedback people' (identified by wearing lanyards) at each event who you can feel free to approach. If you prefer you can contact the [Fetlife page](https://fetlife.com/RopesinSpace) or use our [anonymous feedback form](https://cryptpad.fr/form/#/2/form/view/2Kucmewitfv0oagyICsxCB-IBkiVIi0zs49H5VQJM1k/)
